Bullet Operator Alt Code and Symbol

The Alt code for Bullet Operator is 249. Hold Alt, type 249 on the numeric keypad, then release Alt. Bullet Operator also has the Unicode codepoint U+2219, so you can type it with Alt+8729 on Windows, search for U+2219 in macOS's Character Viewer, use ∙ in HTML, or \2219 in CSS. If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly — the Alt key method requires a physical numpad. Copy the Bullet Operator character from this page when you need it in a form, chat message or document that does not accept Alt codes. Bullet Operator has no named HTML entity, so use the numeric escape ∙ or the hex escape ∙.

How to type bullet operator on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 2 4 9 on the numeric keypad.
  4. Release Alt. The Bullet Operator character (∙) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type bullet operator on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Bullet Operator. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Bullet Operator" and click the character to insert it.

How to use bullet operator in code

  • HTML: or
  • CSS: content:"\2219"; ()
  • Python: \u2219 or chr(0x2219)
  • JavaScript: \u2219 or String.fromCodePoint(0x2219)
  • JSON: "\u2219"

Frequently asked questions

What is the Alt code for Bullet Operator?

The legacy Alt code for Bullet Operator is 249. Hold Alt, type 2 4 9 on the numeric keypad, then release Alt.

How do I type ∙ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ∙, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+8729 not work?

Alt+8729 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Bullet Operator?

The Unicode codepoint for Bullet Operator is U+2219. You can use this value in HTML as ∙, in CSS as \2219, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ∙ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+2219, then click it.
